playbook:
When I open with KING, I bet to apply pressure and build the pot.

When I open with QUEEN, I bet to seize initiative and force folds unless table or stack conditions strongly favor a trap; when facing a bet into my QUEEN, I call rather than fold.

When I open with JACK, I check by default; I only bet J as an exploit if I am significantly behind on chips and the opponent has shown a high frequency of folding to unchecked openings.

When the opponent checks to me, I bet with KING or QUEEN to try to take the pot; I only check-back with JACK.

When the opponent bets into my check with a JACK, I fold to avoid paying to see a stronger card unless the pot odds or reads justify a call.

When I am behind in chips, I increase aggression with KINGs and QUEENs (more frequent bets) to try to recover; when I am ahead I tighten marginally—still bet KING, bet QUEEN but avoid unnecessary bluffs with JACK.

At showdown I always truthfully declare the card I was dealt (do not lie or name anything other than JACK, QUEEN, or KING).

When deciding between calling and folding to a bet, prefer calling with QUEEN and KING; prefer folding with JACK unless explicit pot odds or reads recommend calling.
